query: For MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials, what single intervention could improve mechanical performance while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected changes relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Partial substitution of Si with Ge in MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials will improve mechanical performance (e.g., ductility and fracture toughness) while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect, due to enhanced lattice stability and minimal disruption of the magnetostructural transition.
generation.material_initial_state: MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration alloy in its standard composition (without Ge substitution).
generation.intervention: Partial substitution of Si with Ge (e.g., MnNiSi1-xGex, with x ≈ 0.1–0.2).
generation.conditions: Room temperature to near the magnetostructural transition temperature; ambient pressure; polycrystalline bulk samples.
generation.structural_mediator: Ge substitution increases lattice parameter and stabilizes the crystal structure, reducing brittleness and improving mechanical properties, while preserving the first-order magnetostructural transition responsible for the magnetocaloric effect.
generation.mechanism: Ge atoms, being larger than Si, expand the lattice and reduce internal stresses, leading to improved mechanical performance. The similar electronic structure of Ge and Si allows the magnetocaloric effect to be retained, as the magnetostructural transition remains sharp and large.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to baseline MnNiSi, MnNiSi1-xGex alloys will show higher fracture toughness and ductility, with only minor reduction (if any) in the peak magnetic entropy change (ΔSm) and adiabatic temperature change (ΔTad).
generation.baseline: MnNiSi alloy without Ge substitution, known for large magnetocaloric effect but poor mechanical performance (brittleness).
generation.boundary: If Ge content exceeds a threshold (x > 0.2), the magnetocaloric effect may decrease significantly or the magnetostructural transition may broaden, reducing performance.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of mechanical improvement and exact retention of magnetocaloric effect depend on precise Ge content and synthesis conditions; insufficient prior evidence for quantitative prediction.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare MnNiSi and MnNiSi1-xGex (x = 0.1–0.2) samples. Measure mechanical properties (fracture toughness, ductility) and magnetocaloric effect (ΔSm, ΔTad) near the magnetostructural transition.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If MnNiSi1-xGex alloys do not show improved mechanical properties compared to MnNiSi, or if the magnetocaloric effect (ΔSm, ΔTad) drops by more than 20% relative to baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
